description:
Price context for a tradable ticker (stock / ETF / index-ETF / forex / crypto / commodity), split &
    dividend-ADJUSTED — a DIGESTED read, NOT a raw bar series: windowed changes (1w/1mo/3mo/ytd/1y), 52-week
    range + `drawdown_from_52w_high_pct` (how far below the peak), realized vol + `realized_vol_percentile_1y`
    (is today's vol high vs its OWN year), trend vs SMA50/200, volume conviction (`up_down_volume_ratio_1mo`,
    rvol). `*_read` fields are ready plain-language labels — quote them, don't re-derive. Reach for this on
    "is it cheap/extended / how has it moved / why is it dropping" — the LEVEL that makes a news+options read
    actionable (or use `pulse(kind='asset')` to get price + news + options in one). `to` = as-of date (point-in-time,
    YYYY-MM-DD, features as of that day); `from_` bounds history (narrowing below ~1y nulls the long windows).
    For a SECTOR/theme (not one ticker) use `pulse(kind='theme')`, not this. 🔵 BONDS/RATES: if `metric_kind` ==
    "yield" (a `.GB` govt-bond yield like US-10Y.GB or a `.MM` rate like SOFR.MM) the stored value is a
    LEVEL, not a price — narrate each window's `change_bps` in BASIS POINTS, NOT `change_pct` (a % of a
    yield is sign-inverted + the wrong unit; e.g. US-10Y 1y = "+52 bps", not "+12%"). Bonds also carry
    per-window `price_proxy_pct` + top-level `mod_duration` = an L1 bond-PRICE estimate (≈ −ModDur×Δy) for
    "the bond fell ~4%" narration (label it an ESTIMATE; for an exact bond return point to a bond ETF like
    TLT/IEF). Volume fields (`rvol`, `up_down_volume_ratio_1mo`, …) are `null` for a yield — don't present
    volume conviction; and yield↑ ⇒ bond price↓.

context.description: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED — paste the user's FULL request VERBATIM (any language: 'ขอราคาผลไม้ apple', 'compare Apple and Microsoft stock'). The server uses it to disambiguate which candidate each `ticker` entity means (the apple COMPANY vs the fruit COMMODITY; which Samsung). One context per call, shared by all tickers here.
context.title: Context

country.description: OPTIONAL market disambiguator — pass ONLY when `ticker` is a plain NAME that collides across markets (the Thai vs Korean 'KBANK'); omit for a distinctive name or an exact ticker (an unneeded country silently 0-matches). A country NAME or ISO-2 code ('South Korea'/'KR'); the server normalizes, so pass the NAME when unsure — never GUESS a 2-letter code ('CH' = Switzerland, not China).
country.title: Country

from_.description: Lower bound of price history `YYYY-MM-DD`. Narrowing below ~1y nulls the long windows. Price history goes back DECADES (unlike news, 2026+).
from_.title: From

ticker.description: A Ava Advisor ticker OR a company/asset NAME — the SERVER resolves it (no lookup step). A COMPANY/proper NAME passes AS-IS in any language (茅台/トヨタ/삼성 resolve natively — never translate a name); a generic COMMODITY/SECTOR concept must be ENGLISH (黄金→'gold', 原油→'crude oil'). Pass the user's full request in `context` to disambiguate ('apple' company vs fruit); if still ambiguous you get a `needs_confirmation` with candidates — resolve from conversation or ask, then re-call. Exact tickers pass through (Ava Advisor suffixes: Korea .KO, Taiwan .TW, commodity .COMM, crypto .CC, FX .FOREX, bond .GB, rate .MM).
ticker.title: Ticker

to.description: As-of date `YYYY-MM-DD` — features computed as of that day (point-in-time). Omit → latest.
to.title: To
